summary: This paper demonstrates that simultaneous high-fidelity readout ($F \geq 99\%$, $\mathrm{SNR}^2 \geq 282$) and strong coupling ($g_s \geq \kappa$) are achievable in donor-based flip-flop qubits coupled to superconducting resonators by optimizing the tunnel coupling $V_t$. The authors rigorously map the competing trade-offs between spin-photon coupling strength, qubit relaxation, and readout efficiency, showing that intermediate $V_t \approx 2\pi \times (10$–$16)$ GHz provides the widest operational window, with squeezed input fields offering a practical route to relax experimental constraints on charge-photon coupling $g_c$ and photon loss $\kappa$.
motivation: Scaling spin qubits via circuit QED requires strong spin-photon coupling for long-range interactions and high-fidelity readout, but spin-charge hybridization—necessary to generate an electric dipole moment—introduces competing decoherence and relaxation channels that degrade readout performance. This work identifies optimal operating points that balance these fundamental constraints in the flip-flop qubit platform.
method: The authors perform Schrieffer-Wolff transformations to derive the dispersive Hamiltonian, account for valley-enhanced phonon-mediated relaxation ($\gamma_{\mathrm{FF}}$ following Eq. 15 with $\Theta = 2.37 \times 10^{-24}$ s$^2$) and Purcell decay ($\gamma_{\mathrm{pu}} \approx g_s^2 \kappa / \Delta_-^2$), and use input-output theory to calculate the readout SNR and signal-to-noise ratio-limited fidelity. They systematically map the parameter space ($\epsilon$, $V_t$, $g_c$, $\kappa$) against critical photon numbers and validity constraints to identify regimes where both metrics are simultaneously optimized.
result: For realistic parameters ($g_c = 2\pi \times 75$ MHz, $\kappa = 2\pi \times 0.325$ MHz), simultaneous strong coupling and $F \geq 99\%$ fidelity is accessible at $V_t \approx 2\pi \times (10$–$16)$ GHz with no squeezing; modest squeezing ($r \approx 0.37$–$2.3$) extends this window and enables $F \approx 99.3\%$ at higher $V_t$, demonstrating that experimentally achievable squeezing (currently $\sim 15$ dB) can bridge the $g_c$ and $\kappa$ bottlenecks for scalable cQED architectures.
